They weigh exactly the same — a kilogram is a unit of mass, not weight, so a kilogram of feathers and a kilogram of steel both have a mass of one kilogram. (In common usage, "weight" is often used to mean "mass," but in physics, "weight" refers to the force of gravity acting on a mass, which varies with location.)
